Anchors resolved in reference_text() (resolve=last→rfind; <<EOF>>=EOF). structure=repeating ⇒ expected_count+count_cue carry cardinality (A3 scores recall-of-count, not exact edges); exemplars anchor concrete instances. role=primary drives the rating; role=secondary is a grouping level reported but not rated. annotations.count_cue: Part II ('Texts and Translations', body from offset ~539971) is a critical edition: each excerpted Armenian source-text is given as a numbered ORIGINAL passage in Armenian script (U+0530–058F, 19.4% of the whole file) immediately followed by its ENGLISH translation, plus a 'Text:'/'Translation:'/'See also:' citation header per source. The masked-translation layer is keyed at the SOURCE-ENTRY level: 121 author/source entries, matching exactly the 'Alphabetical List of Authors Cited' (front, -xv-) and 'Alphabetical List of Authors Quoted' (back) — both enumerate 121 author headers (regex /\n<Name> C\d+/ over each list = 121, cross-validated front vs back). The PASSAGE count is HIGHER and NOT cleanly countable from reference_text(): 169 'Text:' labels (some inline sub-works), 98 '§N' source-section refs, and many entries hold several numbered excerpts; an Armenian-para→English-para transition scan over Part II yields ~782 (noisy — single passages span multiple paragraphs). So expected_count=121 is the verifiable SOURCE-entry cardinality, not the passage cardinality (flagged honestly). DETECTOR EMITS ZERO translations (by_type has no 'translation') → recall 0 → MIRAGE: composite 100 over a 472K-char parallel-text edition the detector sees as undifferentiated body.

annotations.note: TYPE JUDGMENT (Armenian original vs English translation vs commentary): the taxonomy has no clean 'original-language' type. The Armenian-script passages are the ORIGINAL; I do NOT give them a separate annotation — they sit inside the same source-entry as their translation and are masked together as the body of the edition. The ENGLISH renderings are typed `translation` (the high-value masked layer this gold exists to surface). Per-source citation headers ('Text:'/'Translation:'/'See also:') and the numbered excerpt apparatus are part of these entries. Distinct from `commentary` (Part I analytic prose) and from `footnotes` (the numbered note apparatus).

annotations.count_cue: Part I ('The Adam and Eve Traditions in Armenian', body PART I @ ~22692) is the scholarly analysis: 5 numbered chapters (Fifth-Century; Sixth–Eleventh; Twelfth–Thirteenth; Fourteenth–Fifteenth; Sixteenth–Seventeenth Armenian Literature) + 1 Appendix ('Satan and the Serpent', -177-) = 6 analytic units, English prose with inline Armenian-script quotations. Count is TOC-exact (printed Contents lists chapters 1–5 + Appendix). `commentary` is mask=False (unmasked content type) per taxonomy. Detector emits no `commentary` → these read as plain body. NOTE: the discussion-vs-commentary call: the taxonomy also has `discussion` (mask=True); I chose `commentary` because the content is sustained authorial scholarly commentary on the source texts, and commentary is the registered unmasked analytic type.

annotations.count_cue: Dense scholarly footnote apparatus throughout: numbered notes 'N.\u2002<text>' (number + EN-SPACE U+2002) keyed to inline superscript digits in both the analytic prose (Part I) and the translations (Part II). A '\nN.\u2002' line-start scan yields 2512 hits across the file, but the per-chapter/per-page numbering RESTARTS, so no single global count is meaningful and notes are NOT uniquely content-anchorable (e.g. cross-references repeat). expected_count=null: presence + masked layer is the contract, not a global cardinality.
annotations.note: Masked annotation apparatus the linear extraction interleaves into body/commentary/translation. Detector emits no `footnotes`.
